The Roadmap Ahead

📅 Nov 28, 2026  |  Category: Technology  |  Read Source →

Chaiwat Nookleang/iStock via Getty Images

Chaiwat Nookleang/iStock via Getty Images

The S&P 500 Index is topping. Gold and silver are bottoming. It's a process. In our view, both sides of the trade have never been more attractive in terms of valuation and timing.

The S&P 500 finally experienced a significant correction last week. The volatility index (VIX) spiked to almost 40 last Friday. With the S&P 500 down more than 8% that week and volatility so high, we booked significant short-term profits on our S&P 500 put portfolio in our macro and long/short funds on Friday. With President Trump reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO of Nvidia on Monday and the massive short-covering rally in big tech that followed, we began layering those puts back in and became fully positioned on the short side again yesterday. We have had several days this month when these three funds have been up while the S&P 500 has been down.

In bear markets, put portfolios need to be tactically traded. There is no guarantee we will be successful on the short side going forward, but we have high conviction that there is much more to play out on the downside for the stock market at large. We have been minimizing the risk of shorting the market through put options while preserving the asymmetric reward-to-risk upside potential to a further downturn in the S&P 500 in these three funds. These are lessons learned by Crescat's founder and CEO in managing hedge funds through the 2000s tech bust and the 2008 Global Financial Crisis.

Meanwhile, our activist metals mining stock portfolio has experienced a significant pullback in line with the precious metals markets. We believe the precious metals complex is in deep oversold territory, on par with other major V-bottoms historically, not unlike in the depths of the 2008 GFC and the 2020 Covid crash.

There are three notable historical precedents for our primary macro investment thesis today: the deflationary Great Depression, the stagflationary bear market of 1973-74, and the bursting of the technology bubble in 2000. In each of these periods, the premier gold mining stocks appreciated substantially while the broader equity market suffered major declines. While not all gold mining companies were successful in these periods and risk remains, we believe the following three macro charts highlight the parallels we find ourselves in today and provide the roadmap for what lies ahead.

In the deflationary Great Depression, Homestake Mining (HM) was the largest gold mining company in the US and dramatically outperformed the Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA). From the DJIA's high in September 1929 to its low in July 1932, it lost 89% of its value, yet HM's stock price was up 48%. By February 1936, HM shares had gained 580% while the DJIA was still down 59% from its top.

During the stagflationary stock market slide of 1973 and 1974, the S&P 500 fell 48% from its high in January 1973 to its low in October 1974, a period over which the Barronâs Gold Mining Index (BGMI) rose 193%. Notably, the BGMI began rising almost two months before the S&P 500 peaked and continued rising during the ensuing bear market. From its low in November 1972 to its intermediate high in August 1974, the BGMI was up 376%, while the S&P 500 was down 34% over the same period.

The early innings of the 2000 tech bust marked the end of a two-decade bear market for precious metals mining stocks. From its high in October 1980 to its low in November 2000, the BGMI fell 82% while the S&P 500 gained 985% over the same period.

The worst of that bear market for mining stocks occurred from 1996 to 2000, when technology stocks were booming, potentially not unlike today. As the technology bubble burst, a new secular bull market for precious metals mining stocks began. From November 2000 to March 2008, the Philadelphia Gold and Silver Index (XAU) gained 393% while the Nasdaq Composite declined 27%.

With the S&P 500 trading near historic valuations, we believe our Global Macro Fundâs long-term track record is particularly relevant today. Since its inception in January 2006, the fund has generated a net annualized return of 9.1% with a downside capture ratio of -15.6% relative to the S&P 500 through September 2026. The chart below illustrates how rare this combination of strong absolute returns and negative downside capture has been among our discretionary global macro peers over the period.

In our October investor letter, we highlighted the valuation disconnect between precious metals explorers and gold. We think the chart below is worth revisiting as the recent pullback has only made the opportunity more attractive.

During previous gold bull markets, exploration equities traded at substantially higher multiples relative to gold than they do today. Despite gold trading at multiples of its previous cycle highs, the S&P/TSX Venture Index remains a fraction of the levels it reached in 2007 and 2011. There is tremendous catching up to do.

Over the last seven years, we have curated our activist metals portfolio with the help of geologic experts. It includes many of what we believe are the world's most exciting new, large precious and critical metals discoveries. Our conviction in these companies has not changed, and we expect the biggest upside yet in our portfolio is still ahead of us.

We derive a price target for gold of $20,000 per troy ounce based on two independent macro models. The first looks at the trend of global M2 money supply compared to the above-ground gold stock as shown in the chart below. With the precious metal now under accumulation by global central banks, we think this chart is highly relevant. Extending the trendline points to a price target for gold of $20,000 in approximately four years, though we suspect global M2 could accelerate given the current fiscal imbalances and geopolitical climate to shorten this timeline.

Our second approach to the target price for gold uses a gold-to-S&P 500 ratio model and assumes a run-of-the-mill US stock market decline of 50% and an ensuing dollar devaluation. Starting from historic large cap equity valuations today and record fiscal imbalances, we believe such a path could once again lie ahead. Each of the prior peaks in this ratio was catalyzed by a stock market crash from historic large cap equity valuations and a substantial dollar devaluation. A 50% lower S&P 500, combined with a 5.25 gold-to-S&P 500 multiple, which is well below its 1980 peak of 7.58, though slightly above its 1933 peak of 4.76, also gets us to our $20,000 price target for gold.

A market top may have already happened or could be forming very soon. The time window from the peak of the stock market to the ensuing peak in the gold price was only 4.3 years from September 1929 to January 1934. It took 7 years from January 1973 to January 1980.

Our activist metals portfolio remains the largest long investment theme across our five hedge funds. As shown below, we currently have US$412 million in exposure across 61 positions, including 30 companies with bona fide discoveries using the Newmont criteria (3 or more 100 gram-meter intercepts on a gold equivalent basis). Most of our companies are public, but we have 13 private companies. We have ownership stakes exceeding 5% on a partially diluted basis in 45 companies, with median firmwide partially diluted ownership of 9.1%.

We expect our portfolio companies to have 102 drills operating over the next 12 months, including substantially more greenfield drilling than all the major mining producers combined. Collectively, based on our geologic estimates, our companies have identified 256 million target gold-equivalent ounces of precious and critical metals in viable US-friendly mining jurisdictions around the world. In our strong view, these include many of the new tier-1 metal discoveries and deposits that the major mining companies will need to acquire in order to extend their reserves. The major mining companies have under-invested in new resource development for the past 15 years. As a result, the industry is facing a supply cliff. We believe Crescat's portfolio companies will contribute substantially to the new supply that the world needs.

The activist metals portfolio subset consists of firmwide holdings across all Crescat funds and SMA accounts in the mining industry where Crescat strives to help companies build economic metal resources through exploration and drilling. For some companies, Crescat provides capital and geologic guidance to help companies build resources across Crescat's activist portfolio.

Crescat target resource estimates are based on internal modeling and geologic estimates, and include various assumptions based on analysis of geology, geophysics, geochemistry, historic drill assays, and metallurgical recovery data received to date. Target resource estimates are discounted based on drilling progress to date, an assessment of the management and technical team's strengths and weaknesses affecting their ability to advance the project, and environmental, local community, and government permitting risk factors. Estimates are displayed on a gold equivalent basis based on current price-to-gold ratios for silver, copper, and other metals if the primary metal is other than gold. The S&P 500 is still valued near record all-time highs across a variety of measures, including Shiller CAPE ratio, market cap-to-GDP, EV-to-sales, EV-to-free cash flow, and price-to-book. Don't overthink it! In our strong view, as the reflexive circular financing that drove AI capex bubble goes into reverse and drives the AI bust, it's extremely positive for our short S&P 500 and long precious and critical metals mining thesis. That's because we believe the Fed will cut interest rates and embark on its biggest inflationary money printing yet in 2027. By stark contrast, the Fed funds futures market today is still pricing in two-and-a-half more Fed rate hikes (and implicitly zero QE) over the next year. Crescat's founder and CEO thinks this is the biggest mismatch in Fed expectations versus plausible reality that he has ever seen. It is a rare setup that we believe will prove explosive to the upside for gold prices in the months and years ahead.

Across Crescat's five funds, we have built a portfolio of what we believe to be some of the biggest and best new major gold, silver, and copper discoveries in safe US-friendly mining jurisdictions around the world. We believe our activist metals portfolio is deeply undervalued. Our small-cap, high-growth, exploration-focused companies have been flying under the radar of the general investing public. Many of our small-cap companies have already made large-cap discoveries, in terms of the potential future mineable metal value they have identified through drilling. Based on the estimates of our geologic expert, Bill Pearson, PhD, we believe the intrinsic value of our portfolio companies is worth many multiples of where the market currently values them.

At Crescat, we have built an activist metals portfolio that we believe has outstanding upside relative to gold for the current macro environment. Our metals portfolio propelled us to five of the top sixteen performing hedge funds in the world in 2025, according to the Preqin database1. We are determined to do something like that again in 2027 and beyond. The pullback in precious metals in 2026 is way overdone, in our strong opinion. It presents an excellent opportunity to deploy capital into Crescat's funds now. Yes, the precious and critical metals markets are volatile, but the potential upside for the macro environment ahead more than justifies the risk, in our strong view.

The opportunities to rotate out of mega cap tech and into undervalued new growth sectors of the market are not just limited to precious and critical metals miners. We see extraordinary opportunity in biotechnology as well, which we view as part of the defensive health care sector. As a reminder, the Crescat Biotech Fund is launching on January 1, 2027. We believe we are in the early stages of a new biotech investment cycle following a prolonged post-pandemic correction. The sector offers attractive valuations, accelerating biomedical innovation, and a looming patent expiration cliff facing big pharma that we believe will drive M&A activity.

Our investment focus is on late-stage clinical and emerging commercial companies developing transformational therapies, with an emphasis on identifiable value-creating catalysts such as Phase II and III clinical trial results, FDA approvals, commercial launches, strategic partnerships, and pharmaceutical mergers and acquisitions.

Lars Eyde Theill, PhD, will serve as portfolio manager. Lars has 35 years of biotech experience, including 15 years at Amgen. He has helped advise Crescatâs biotech investment theme since its inception in January 2023 and will continue to advise the biotech sleeves within our Global Macro and Long/Short funds alongside the new dedicated Biotech Fund.

From January 1, 2023, through September 30, 2026, Crescatâs biotech investment theme generated a gross annualized return of 26.5% and a cumulative gross return of 141.4%, outperforming both the S&P Biotech Select and NYSE Biotech benchmarks over the period. Star Trek: Enterprise-Q Officially Reunites The Next Generation Crew

📅 Nov 28, 2026  |  Category: Technology  |  Read Source →

It's been a roller-coaster ride of a year for Star Trek's 60th anniversary, with some major ups and downs given Sir Patrick Stewart's passing last month. However, the franchise has certainly given fans plenty to celebrate, with a slew of major announcements and official releases across virtually every entertainment medium imaginable.

From the fourth season of Strange New Worlds and the debut of Starfleet Academy to original digital comics, new novels, video games, and even official LEGO collaborations, there's been something for practically every generation of Star Trek fans throughout 2026.

Of course, for longtime fans of Star Trek: The Next Generation, there's something particularly bittersweet about revisiting the adventures of Captain Jean-Luc Picard and his crew in light of Stewart's passing. Fortunately, one of the latest official anniversary releases, Enterprise-Q, reunites several of the Enterprise's most beloved crew members alongside one of the franchise's most iconic antagonists.

As part of the massive Magic: The Gathering and Star Trek Universes Beyond crossover, Wizards of the Coast has released a special Enterprise-Q Scene Box that reunites several of the most iconic characters from The Next Generation, with a hilarious twist courtesy of John de Lancie's beloved Q.

The collection features six unique borderless cards illustrated by artist Alexander Gering that, when arranged together, form one large panoramic illustration of the Enterprise's bridge. Unsurprisingly, Q is up to his usual antics, much to the apparent dismay of Captain Picard and his fellow Starfleet officers.

There are six iconic Star Trek: The Next Generation characters featured in the Enterprise-Q collection, including the following:

What's great about the collection is how they've incorporated Q's reality-altering abilities into the actual gameplay mechanics. The six legendary creatures are designed around Faerie synergies, with Q himself serving as a five-color Commander.

The Enterprise-Q Scene Box retails for $41.99 and includes traditional foil versions of all six playable cards, six additional art-only cards, a display easel, and three Star Trek Play Boosters. Non-foil versions of the six playable cards can also be found in Collector Boosters.

This collection is only scratching the surface of what the larger Magic: The Gathering crossover has to offer longtime Next Generation fans. From additional appearances by Picard and his crew to cards featuring the Borg, iconic Federation starships, and even artwork showcasing Data's confrontation with Locutus, there's a ridiculous amount of TNG callbacks across the release.

The crossover also celebrates virtually every era of Star Trek history, with characters from The Original Series, Deep Space Nine, Voyager, and more getting their own official treatments. The Enterprise-Q Scene Box and the wider Magic: The Gathering x Star Trek collection officially launched on November 13 and are available now.

The First AI Stock I Plan to Buy in 2027

📅 Nov 28, 2026  |  Category: Technology  |  Read Source →

Investors should still be considering the world's most popular AI stock.

By Ryan Vanzo – Nov 28, 2026 at 12:00AM EST

Volatility continues for artificial intelligence (AI) stocks. Long-term investors should view today's market conditions as an opportunity.

The AI opportunity isn't going anywhere. Experts still forecast sizable demand growth for years, if not decades, to come.

"As we prepare to turn the page on 2026, the data center build-out continues at full throttle," research from Boston Consulting Group concludes. "Yet even spending at this rate is not enough to meet the growing need for DC supply, brought about by the rising adoption of agentic AI," the firm warns. Boston Consulting Group "still expects the high rate of spending to continue through 2031."

Right now is the perfect time for patient investors to shop the AI stock bargain bin. And there's one popular AI stock every investor should strongly consider as a core portfolio position.

If AI spending remains elevated for years to come, Nvidia (NVDA +0.80%) becomes a promising core position for most growth-oriented investors.

But isn't Nvidia facing a lot of uncertainty right now? Absolutely. And that's exactly why shares look attractive.

On paper, everything is going right for Nvidia. As mentioned, the scale of AI spending forecasts remains strong, even if the exact pace is currently in question. The GPU maker holds a sizable market share in AI data centers, and its industry-leading margins indicate that the market views its products as superior.

Meanwhile, pricing and revenue potential of future chip architectures appear strong. CEO Jensen Huang recently revealed that Nvidia's next-gen Vera Rubin chips will generate $40 billion in revenue per gigawatt, up from just $25 billion per gigawatt for Nvidia's Grace Blackwell chips. Morgan Stanley estimates that a Vera Rubin VR200 rack will be priced at roughly $7.8 million, up from roughly $4 million for a GB300 rack.

To be clear, Nvidia faces meaningful near-term uncertainty. Will Huang remain as CEO for the long term? How impactful will regulatory actions and export restrictions be to Nvidia's bottom line? Can AI firms train competing chip architectures to be just as productive, or even end up producing their own chips in-house?

A negative answer to any one of these questions could significantly lower Nvidia's valuation. But at 17 times earnings, most of the uncertainty is arguably already priced in. Nvidia -- the world's biggest and highest-quality chip producer that operates in a multi-year, perhaps even a multi-decade growth window -- now trades at less than 10 times forward earnings. A share buyback program with $227 billion remaining could compound investor returns if shares are indeed severely undervalued.

I expect Nvidia shares to be highly volatile in the coming weeks and months, given ongoing uncertainty. There's no guarantee that today's valuation won't get even cheaper. But if it does, Nvidia will quickly move from an attractive investment candidate to my top stock pick for 2027.

HBO Max just got a family friendly adventure led by Andrew Garfield as a dad you can't help but root for. And "Reacher" star Alan Ritchson teams up with Owen Wilson in an action thriller on Hulu.

It's a sure bet for Best Documentary at the 2027 Oscars with a remarkable 97% on Rotten Tomatoes. If it were me, I'd wait until it comes to HBO Max in early 2027 — and save your hard-earned cash for the next entry in this list.

In our "You Can See Everything" review, my colleague called it "a bold, innovative documentary from alt-comedy creator Nathan Fielder and nonfiction filmmaker Lance Oppenheim, offering a fascinating look at convicted fraudster Elizabeth Holmes." The notorious tech-industry scammer has an acute allergy to self-reflection and proves nearly as manipulative as Fielder himself as the two get closer with the clock ticking down to her prison sentence.

Buy or rent "You Can See Everything" on Amazon now

Sign up to the weekly Tom's Streaming Guide to stay in the loop with the latest releases and top recommendations across your favorite streaming services. We’ve got you covered with a complete guide on what’s worth watching.

Now if you're dead set on relieving yourself of $25 to "own" a movie, "Wicker" is the clear choice for the horniest among us. I saw this in theaters with the girlies, and oh, how we cackled. Olivia Colman is as darling as ever as the prickly fisherwoman, who shows up at the local basket weaver's (Peter Dinklage) door with a weird ask. One wicker husband, coming up!

Alexander Skarsgård is uncanny and charming as her (and the town's) new obsession. Until things go sideways once a little wicker baby shows up...with another woman. "Wicker" is a delightfully horny time, theatrical as all get out, and Dinklage is given leave to soliloquy to his hearts' content. What more could you ask for to wile away a chilly weekend evening?

I'm not the biggest WWII movie buff, but my husband's excited to queue this one up if he can take a break from his emotional support WWII documentaries. A new war drama based on Buzz Bissinger’s nonfiction book of the same name, "The Mosquito Bowl" follows four college football stars who join the swell of promising young lads enlisting in the United States Marine Corps after Pearl Harbor.

With the Battle of Okinawa on the horizon, the guys — played by Nicholas Galitzine, Bill Skarsgård, Ray Nicholson and Tom Francis — stage a football game that would become known as "The Mosquito Bowl" that proves a welcome break from the daily horror of the frontlines. "Friday Night Lights" and "Lone Survivor" director Peter Berg is at the helm of this one, so you know you're in for something memorable, at the very least.

When Tim (Andrew Garfield) and Polly (Claire Foy) move their family of five to the English countryside hoping for a simpler life, their children chance upon an enchanted tree full of kooky inhabitants that can transport them to dazzling new lands befit of a child's imagination. Based on Enid Blyton's beloved children's books, it stars Nicola Coughlan, Nonso Anozie and Jessica Gunning, with a screenplay penned by Paddington 2 co-writer Simon Farnaby.

I haven't seen this one yet, but name-drop "Paddington 2" and you know I'm sat. It's one of the greatest family movies ever made and the rare children's movie I will stand 10-toes down on. If "The Magic Faraway Tree" captures even an ounce of that same magic, we're in for a treat. Plus, Andrew Garfield never fails to be dreamy in these kinds of roles.

Watch "The Magic Faraway Tree" on HBO Max now

"Reacher" star Alan Ritchson has been popping up everywhere lately. He joins forces with Owen Wilson in Hulu's latest action-comedy "Runner" where he gets plenty of opportunities to throw a punch. Ritchson stars as Hank Malone, a former soldier thrown into a frantic race against the clock when a medical delivery lands him squarely in the crosshairs of a ruthless cartel. With an innocent child's life hanging in the balance, Hank's determined to get his cargo where it needs to go before it's too late.

Owen Wilson co-stars as his partner, alongside Rodrigo Santoro as a cartel member and Leila George, with Scott Waugh of "Need for Speed" and "Expend4bles" fame in the director's chair. "Reacher's" really been on a downward trend since season one, but Ritchson and Wilson play off each other well enough in this breezy popcorn watch. And that's exactly the kind of thing that's calling my name after inhaling Thanksgiving dinner.

Moon phase today: What the Moon will look like on November 28, 2026

📅 Nov 28, 2026  |  Category: Technology  |  Read Source →

The Moon is looking noticeably less full now, although most of its surface is still illuminated. We're still in the Waning Gibbous phase, with the Moon getting a little smaller each night as we head towards the Third Quarter.

As of Saturday, Nov. 28, the NASA's Daily Moon Guide tracker tells us the Moon is in the Waning Gibbous phase, with 81% of its surface visible.

If you don't have any visual aids, you can still see the Mares Serenitatis, Oceanus Procellarum, as well as the Tycho Crater. With binoculars, you'll also see the Gassendi Crater, the Clavius Crater, and the Archimedes Crater. And if you have a telescope, you'll get to see all this plus the Apollo 11 and 15 landing spots, plus the Fra Mauro Highlands.

In North America, the next Full Moon will take place on December 23. In other time zones it will fall on December 24.

It takes around 29.5 days for the Moon to move through all its phases, according to NASA. Throughout this period, the Moon's position relative to Earth and the Sun determines how much of its illuminated surface we can see. Starting with a New Moon, the visible portion gradually increases until it reaches a Full Moon, before shrinking again as the cycle comes back around.

New Moon - The Moon is between Earth and the sun, so the side we see is dark (in other words, it's invisible to the eye).

Waxing Crescent - A small sliver of light appears on the right side (Northern Hemisphere).

First Quarter - Half of the Moon is lit on the right side. It looks like a half-Moon.

Waxing Gibbous - More than half is lit up, but it's not quite full yet.

Full Moon - The whole face of the Moon is illuminated and fully visible.

Waning Gibbous - The Moon starts losing light on the right side. (Northern Hemisphere)

Third Quarter (or Last Quarter) - Another half-Moon, but now the left side is lit.

Waning Crescent - A thin sliver of light remains on the left side before going dark again.

Threats Are Outpacing Auditors. AI Isn't Ready. Let's Fix That Anyway.

📅 Nov 27, 2026  |  Category: Technology  |  Read Source →

Security teams today are staring down a firehose of vulnerability disclosures that grows every year. FIRST (the Forum of Incident Response and Security Teams) initially forecast a record number of CVEs in 2026. Its mid-year update pushed that projection even higher: approximately 66,000 CVEs for the year.

But here's the thing: the raw count almost doesn't matter anymore. What matters is which vulnerabilities are actually exploitable and relevant to your environment. That's a prioritization problem --- which means it's a human review time problem.

That's the part that keeps me up at night.

A June 2026 survey of 168 cybersecurity professionals conducted by Filigran at Infosecurity Europe found that 25% identified validating whether risks are real as one of their biggest time sinks. Another 26% pointed to chasing false positives and low-priority alerts.

Meanwhile, 41% identified AI-powered attacks at scale as their biggest security concern.

So defenders are dealing with an increasingly difficult prioritization problem while worrying about attackers using AI to scale their operations.

You can't hire your way out of every problem. Security teams have limited time, limited resources, and a growing number of findings competing for their attention.

So the obvious answer is "throw AI at it," right?

Let me be blunt: I think most AI-based audit tooling today would fail a production bar. Not because the models are dumb --- because the failure modes are brutal in this specific domain:

Hallucinated findings. An AI that invents a vulnerability isn't just wrong, it costs you engineering hours to debunk. Do that twice and your team ignores the tool forever --- which is worse than having no tool, because now you've got false confidence in your skepticism.

Missed real vulnerabilities. The flip side, and scarier. A missed SQLi in an audit report doesn't just sit there --- it can create the false impression that someone checked and everything is fine.

Non-reproducibility. Same codebase, same prompt, different findings on Tuesday than Monday. How do you regression-test an auditor whose judgment drifts? And how do you distinguish a genuine improvement from a change in model behavior?

No universally trusted evaluation baseline. We still don't have a universally accepted way to answer "was this audit actually good?" That makes evaluating AI auditors particularly difficult. We need reliable ways to measure detection rates, false positives, missed vulnerabilities, and consistency across repeated tests.

None of this is a reason to give up. It's the spec for the problem.

In the same Filigran survey, only 8% of security professionals said they'd trust AI to make security decisions without human approval --- and honestly? Good. I agree with the 92%.

Autonomy is not the goal. Trustworthy assistance is.

To be clear, I'm not anti-AI-in-security --- far from it. I think there's a very real version of this that works, it just looks a lot less sci-fi than "AI pentester replaces your red team":

Notice the pattern: human stays in the loop, everywhere.

That's where I think AI can provide the most value right now: helping security professionals work through more information without handing over accountability and final judgment.

Where I wouldn't trust it independently yet: final sign-off, claims that an application is secure, novel exploit discovery, or anything your signed audit report depends on.

Not because AI can't help there --- because we haven't earned that level of trust yet.

Here's my thesis: LLM-based security auditing can be production-ready, but only if we treat the failure modes above as the core engineering problem instead of a footnote.

That means more than pointing an LLM at a codebase and asking it to find vulnerabilities.

I want to know where these tools genuinely help, where they struggle, and where they simply make things up.

That's what I'm going to work on and --- conveniently --- write about here.

Over to you: Has anyone actually run AI audit tooling against a real codebase? What broke first --- the findings, the reproducibility, or your team's patience with it?

I'd genuinely love to hear how it went. Failures especially.

Full Stack Developer Roadmap 2026: Everything You Need to Learn to Become a Developer

📅 Nov 27, 2026  |  Category: Technology  |  Read Source →

The demand for skilled software developers continues to create opportunities for people who want to build a career in technology. Among the many career paths available, becoming a Full Stack Developer is an attractive option because it allows you to work on both the frontend and backend of web applications.

But where should you start? Should you learn HTML first, jump into React, or begin with backend development?

If you are a student, fresher, or someone planning to switch careers into software development, this practical roadmap will help you understand what to learn, which technologies matter, and how to build the skills required to become a Full Stack Developer in 2026.

A Full Stack Developer works on different layers of a web application.

The frontend is the part users interact with. It includes buttons, forms, navigation, layouts, animations, and other visual elements.

The backend handles application logic, authentication, APIs, data processing, and communication with databases.

A Full Stack Developer understands how these components work together to create a complete application.

For example, when someone logs into an online shopping website, the frontend collects the login details, the backend validates them, and the database stores or retrieves the necessary information.

Understanding this connection is the first step toward becoming a developer.

Before learning advanced frameworks, build a strong foundation in HTML and CSS.

HTML provides the structure of a webpage, while CSS controls its appearance and layout.

Your first practical goal should be to create a personal portfolio website.

Try building a responsive landing page, a simple login form, and a basic product page. These projects will help you understand how websites are structured.

JavaScript is one of the most important technologies for modern web development.

It makes websites interactive and allows developers to build complex frontend and backend applications.

Do not rush through JavaScript just to reach React. A strong understanding of JavaScript makes learning frontend frameworks much easier.

Build small projects such as a calculator, weather application, to-do list, and quiz application.

Once your JavaScript fundamentals are strong, start learning React.

React helps developers create reusable user interface components and build dynamic web applications.

After learning the fundamentals, build a dashboard, task management application, or product listing website.

Focus on understanding component structure and managing application state instead of simply copying tutorials.

Frontend development is only one part of the journey. To become a Full Stack Developer, you also need to understand how the backend works.

Node.js allows developers to use JavaScript for server-side development.

Next, learn Express.js, a popular framework for building backend applications.

Understand routing, middleware, request handling, response handling, and API development.

Try building a backend for your to-do application or a simple user management system.

Most real-world applications need to store and retrieve information.

This is where databases become important.

Learn the fundamentals of SQL and relational databases such as PostgreSQL or MySQL.

You can also explore MongoDB to understand document-based databases.

The goal is not to learn every database immediately. Start with one relational database and understand how applications interact with stored information.

Frontend and backend systems communicate through APIs.

You should understand how REST APIs work, how requests and responses are structured, and how data is exchanged using JSON.

Also learn authentication concepts such as:

Build a simple authentication system as a practical exercise. Understanding these concepts will help you create more complete applications.

Knowing how to write code is not enough. Developers also need to manage their code and collaborate with other people.

Learn Git fundamentals, including commits, branches, merging, and resolving conflicts.

Use GitHub to store your projects and maintain a professional development portfolio.

You should also explore basic deployment so that people can access your applications online.

A live project is often more useful when presenting your skills than a folder of unfinished code.

Instead of building ten similar beginner applications, focus on creating a few complete projects.

Include product listings, search, user authentication, shopping cart functionality, and order management.

Build features for job listings, candidate registration, application tracking, and employer dashboards.

Create user accounts, course listings, learning progress, and content management.

Add task creation, editing, filtering, deadlines, and user-specific dashboards.

Explore messaging, authentication, and real-time communication.

For every project, understand the architecture, explain your technical decisions, and document the challenges you solved.

Once you have developed your technical skills, begin preparing for interviews.

Revise JavaScript fundamentals, React concepts, backend development, database queries, APIs, and basic system design.

Practice explaining your projects clearly.

What is the difference between let, const, and var?

What is the difference between SQL and NoSQL?

What happens when you enter a URL in a browser?

Practice writing code without depending entirely on AI tools or tutorials. Interviewers want to understand your thinking and problem-solving ability.

You do not need to learn every technology in a few weeks.

45 minutes of backend or database learning

30 minutes of revision and interview practice

Adjust the schedule based on your current knowledge and available time.

Consistency, practical experience, and regular revision are more valuable than jumping between multiple technologies without mastering the basics.

One common challenge for aspiring developers is finding organized learning material across different technologies.

Instead of switching between random tutorials, documentation, and interview websites, try following a structured learning approach.

MasterClass Buddy provides technology handbooks, coding resources, interview preparation material, quizzes, and learning resources to help students and developers improve their technical knowledge.

Explore the platform here: https://www.masterclassbuddy.com/

Becoming a Full Stack Developer in 2026 is not about learning every programming language or framework available.

It is about understanding the fundamentals, choosing the right technologies, building real-world projects, and developing the ability to solve problems independently.

Start with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. Move toward React and backend development. Learn databases, APIs, Git, and deployment. Most importantly, keep building projects and improving your technical understanding.

Don't just learn technologies. Learn how to use them to build something meaningful.

Ethical Hacking Tools: A Beginner-Friendly Guide

📅 Nov 27, 2026  |  Category: Technology  |  Read Source →

When you start learning ethical hacking, you will come across many different tools. Some are used to scan networks, some help find website vulnerabilities, and others are designed to analyse passwords and network traffic.

At first, it might seem difficult to understand what all these tools do. But you don't need to learn everything at once. The best way to get started is to understand the purpose of each tool and gradually practise using them.

Ethical hackers use these tools to identify security weaknesses and help organisations protect their systems from cyberattacks.

Let's take a look at some popular ethical hacking tools and how they are used. What Are Ethical Hacking Tools? Ethical hacking tools are software programs used to test the security of websites, computer systems, networks, and applications.

They help security professionals discover vulnerabilities, check open ports, analyse network traffic, test password strength, and identify possible security risks.

These tools are useful for both experienced cybersecurity professionals and beginners who want to develop practical skills. 10 Popular Ethical Hacking Tools

It helps ethical hackers identify devices connected to a network, find open ports, and understand which services are running.

It is one of the best tools to explore when learning the basics of network security.

It captures network traffic and allows security professionals to examine how data travels between devices.

It is commonly used for network troubleshooting, analysing suspicious traffic, and understanding network protocols.

It helps ethical hackers test known vulnerabilities and understand how attackers might exploit weaknesses in a system.

It is particularly useful for learning about vulnerability assessment and penetration testing in authorised environments.

It allows testers to inspect communication between a browser and a web server. This helps them identify possible security issues related to login systems, user inputs, and application behaviour.

Anyone interested in website security should consider learning this tool.

It can help identify problems such as security misconfigurations and other common website weaknesses.

It is also a useful option for beginners who want to explore web application security testing.

It uses password-cracking techniques to identify weak passwords and evaluate password strength.

Ethical hackers use it during authorised security assessments to help organisations improve their password security.

It helps security professionals monitor Wi-Fi networks, analyse wireless traffic, and test wireless security configurations.

It is particularly useful for understanding how Wi-Fi security works and what weaknesses can affect wireless networks.

It checks web servers for outdated software, potentially dangerous files, and common security configuration issues.

It can help ethical hackers identify areas that need further security investigation.

It can perform password-guessing tests against supported network services. Security professionals use it to evaluate password security and identify weaknesses in login protection.

It also helps explain why strong passwords and login attempt restrictions are important.

It comes with many pre-installed security tools that help users perform network scanning, vulnerability testing, wireless security assessments, and other security-related tasks.

Many ethical hacking beginners use Kali Linux as their learning environment. Which Tools Should Beginners Learn First? If you are new to ethical hacking, start with tools that help you understand the basics.

Before moving into advanced security testing, try to learn computer networking, Linux commands, operating systems, basic programming, and common cybersecurity concepts.

Also, practise only in your own lab or on systems where you have permission to perform security testing. Using these tools without authorisation can cause legal problems. Conclusion Ethical hacking tools make it easier to identify vulnerabilities and understand how cyberattacks happen. Each tool has a different purpose, and learning them can help you develop practical cybersecurity skills.

If you are a beginner, don't rush to learn all the tools together. Start with one, understand how it works, and practise regularly.

Over time, you will become more familiar with these tools and gain a better understanding of how ethical hackers protect systems and networks.

Remember, ethical hacking is not just about using tools. It's about understanding security problems and finding the right ways to solve them.

Google News RSS no longer gives you the real publisher URL (reuters.com, techcrunch.com, npr.org), and it never includes the article body text. Worse, the old Base64 decoding trick stopped working once Google switched to opaque AU_yqL tokens.

Before mid-2024, the CBMi... token in Google News RSS URLs was simply a Base64-encoded protobuf containing the plaintext publisher URL.

Today, most fresh articles use an opaque AU_yqL token that has to be exchanged with Google's internal RPC endpoint (batchexecute) using a per-article signature (data-n-a-sg) and timestamp (data-n-a-ts).

What Security Teams Can Monitor for CVE-2026-123168

📅 Nov 27, 2026  |  Category: Technology  |  Read Source →

CVE-2026-123168 is a SolarWinds Serv-U insufficient validation flaw that can escalate a high-privilege application account to root on Linux. SolarWinds fixed it in Serv-U 2026.4. Detection has to work around an important gap: the public advisory does not identify the exact malformed input or vulnerable request.

The GitHub Advisory Database scores the flaw 9.1 with CVSS 3.1 vector AV:N/AC:L/PR:H/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H. The vulnerable interaction is reachable over the network, has low complexity, and requires high privileges. No user interaction is required. An unauthenticated request stream is not the right detection premise.

Monitoring should focus on privileged Serv-U identities and the transition from application activity to host-level behavior. That does not mean every administrator login is suspicious. It means the logs should make an unusual pattern visible before a routine administrative action becomes a host compromise.

Collect authentication events, role changes, administrative actions, service starts, configuration changes, file-transfer metadata, and operating system process or file events from each Serv-U host. Preserve source time, user identity, session identifier, host, and version with the event. A log without an attributable identity or host cannot support a useful investigation.

For Linux, include authentication, sudo, process execution, and file-integrity sources where available. For Windows, include account, service, process, and file audit sources. The exact products vary by environment, but the coverage questions remain: who acted, on which server, with what privilege, and what changed on the host.

High-privilege accounts are part of the exploit condition. Alert on new administrator roles, restored accounts, permission grants, and authentication from unexpected locations. Review dormant privileged users and shared credentials. A login from a known administrator may be normal, while a dormant identity becoming active near a configuration change deserves review.

The public record does not specify whether one particular built-in role is required. Avoid signatures that assume a role name that the sources do not name. Use the vendor's permission model and the local administrative design to define the set of identities with high privilege.

The significant outcome is root access on Linux. Detection should therefore include new processes running as root, unexpected changes to service binaries or configuration, new local users or authorized keys, and modifications to audit or logging configuration. These events are generic because the public exploit detail is absent. A generic signal is still useful when it is correlated with Serv-U identity and session activity.

Do not automatically label a root event as exploitation of this CVE. Legitimate maintenance can produce the same effects. Correlation, change records, and the installed version help separate expected administration from an intrusion.

INCIBE lists Serv-U 2026.3 and earlier as affected. Security telemetry should carry the current Serv-U release so an alert can identify whether the host was patched. The 2026.4 release notes confirm the fix. A log search across unversioned hosts will produce results that cannot be prioritized.

Record the patch state separately from the detection state. A host can have suspicious activity and a current version, or an old version and no observed alert. Each fact answers a different question.

The reused product query returned 370,596 matches for app="SolarWinds Serv-U", and the CVE filter returned 0. The broad count can help identify externally observable instances, but it cannot prove a version, role, or compromise. The zero filter is not evidence that internal monitoring is unnecessary.

External exposure and internal telemetry should be joined through the asset inventory. If an external match corresponds to a known host, verify the version and management path. If no match exists, continue to inspect internal management networks, because non-public instances can still carry the flaw.

For a suspected case, collect the Serv-U version, relevant sessions, role assignments, host authentication, process and file events, configuration changes, and network connections around the alert. Record the collection time and preserve logs before cleanup. The exact malformed request may not be visible, so the investigation should rely on identity, host, and outcome rather than a single packet signature.

The absence of a public exploit signature should not lead teams to invent one. A disciplined packet based on the known privilege boundary is more defensible.

Upgrade to Serv-U 2026.4, verify the installed build, and continue monitoring privileged activity after the update. A patch closes the stated vulnerability. It does not remove the need to control administrative roles or detect root-level changes.

On the first series of the second half, Simmons caught a pass over the middle and turned it into a 32-yard TD.

The first quarter looked like a Thanksgiving nap. Then Tech hung a season-high points yield on the FBS' 16th-ranked scoring defense.

Fumble recoveries by Adam Trick and Peyton Morgan — only Tech's second and third of the season — led to 10 points. LBs Ben Roberts (13 tackles) and Austin Romaine (12 tackles) and DT Julien Laventure (7 tackles, sack) showed the way.

Stone Harrington's two field goals started the comeback. Malcolm Simmons' punt-return TD largely made up for Kenny Johnson's muffed punt.

Shiel Wood and company mostly tightened up the defense after a shaky first quarter. The Mack Leftwich offense continues to evolve as Thomas Castellanos and Simmons settle in more and more.

A short week and a slow start became a moot point. Just like last year, the Red Raiders followed up a mid-October loss with a five-game win streak to end the regular season.

If you replayed The Witcher 3 in its shiny new remastered form and got absolutely bodied by a couple of werewolf fights you thought were easier back when you had more youthful reflexes, don't worry—the problem wasn't your aging brain and hands after all. It was a bug that's been caught and exterminated in patch 5.02. "Fixed an issue where werewolves could regenerate health too quickly on higher difficulty settings," the patch notes say, "making them impossible to defeat."

Another problem some players had with The Witcher 3 Remastered was its lighting, with interiors in particular looking too dark while some other locations were washed-out flashbangs. Good news: "Fixed various lighting issues across multiple locations and cutscenes," the patch notes say, "including overly bright or dark areas, inconsistent lighting transitions and flickering." They've also "Fixed various lighting issues with hair when Path Tracing is enabled" and "Made various Path Tracing and Ray Reconstruction optimizations and visual improvements, including lighting, shadows, and water rendering."

That's all positive stuff, but the balance changes to various signs and mutations will be more controversial. The Remastered version launched with buffs to Witcher signs that made them useful even if you didn't specialize in them, but it may have overdone things a little. This patch walks back some of the potential for you to dominate the entire game with an Aard build, though changes like reducing the Catalyst skill's bonus to Aard and Igni intensity by 10% don't seem like they'll totally change the way you play.

I get that people don't like skill nerfs in singleplayer games, but I can also see CD Projekt anticipating next year's Songs of the Past DLC. They don't want to hear a bunch of players say, "It sucked because I trivialized the whole thing with a broken build I got by copying a YouTuber." If some skill nerfs and a reduction to stamina regeneration in combat mean you have to drink more potions to get your signs off, it probably won't ruin your fun.

Oh, and if you couldn't complete your Gwent collection because Zoltan Chivay's card didn't show up, the patch notes say it'll now appear in the correct place under the Hanged Man's Tree in Velen. Time to go back and get that 100% achievement at last.

The EBA urges the EU to assess restrictions on crypto firms facilitating loans involving USDT and other unauthorized stablecoins.

Tether’s USDT led stablecoin borrowing on Aave, Fluid and Spark in a July 30 snapshot published by the European Banking Authority (EBA) on Nov. 25.

The EBA renewed its call for the European Commission to assess rules for firms that give customers access to decentralized lending, including possible restrictions on loans involving stablecoins that lack the required EU authorization.

In its comparison of six lending protocols, the regulator grouped USDT and its USDT0 bridged version when describing demand on Aave, Fluid and Spark. The EBA also found that borrowers on JustLend overwhelmingly favored USDT and pointed to the token’s dominance on the Tron blockchain.

USDC accounted for a larger share of active loans than USDT on Compound and Morpho.

The EBA measured each stablecoin against all active loans on the same protocol. Separate estimates suggest EU participation in decentralized finance remains limited, and self-hosted wallets and reporting gaps make it difficult to identify where users are based.

The EU’s Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA) requires authorization for covered stablecoins to be offered to the public or admitted to trading in the EU, and USDT lacks that authorization.

The EBA’s summary of MiCA’s scope says fully decentralized services operating without an intermediary fall outside the rules. The report says some EU consumers may hold stablecoins like USDT in wallets they control themselves.

Some crypto firms give customers access to lending protocols through their own interfaces, while others offer products tied to decentralized lending.

The EBA describes arrangements that let customers put their stablecoins to work without opening a self-hosted wallet. In those cases, customers depend on the platform that handles the investment.

China, Japan, South Korea and ASEAN to form working group on digital payments, crypto regulation

Looking for institutional-grade crypto trading? Discover LMAX Digital, the regulated exchange from LMAX Group

The decision comes after the group met in May in Uzbekistan and identified cross-border digital payments as a new area of cooperation.

China, Japan, South Korea, and ASEAN member countries have agreed to set up a dedicated working group on cross-border digital payments and digital asset regulation.

According to a statement released Thursday, finance and central bank deputies gathered in Kyoto, Japan, this week to review progress in implementing the guidance set earlier by the ASEAN+3 finance ministers and central bank governors.

One major focus of the meeting was technological innovation, with discussions centering around cross-border payments and regulatory approaches to crypto assets. The deputies agreed to form the AMRO Cross-Border Digital Payments Program and a dedicated working group to support further policy talks.

The Kyoto decision is a result of a May meeting in Uzbekistan that identified cross-border digital payments as a new area of cooperation.

At that meeting, the group instructed deputies to establish modalities by the end of 2026 to deepen policy discussions on retail and wholesale payment connectivity, as well as regulatory approaches to stablecoins.

"Building on local currency‑based payment systems, technological innovation in cross‑border payments, such as tokenization, should be pursued in consistency with ongoing global discussions on policy […]," the group said in a May statement.

According to AMRO’s job post published last week seeking a consultant on cross-border retail payments, the initiative could cover research into a range of use cases, including person-to-person and person-to-merchant payments, tourism, e-commerce, and remittances.

Finance ministers and central bank governors are expected to further discuss the matter at the next meeting in Nagoya, Japan, in May 2027.

ASEAN+3 is an international cooperation framework that brings together 11 ASEAN member states and China, Japan, and South Korea. The 14 economies regularly convene to discuss political-security, economic, and socio-cultural matters.

The push for closer regional cooperation comes as Asian economies step up efforts to explore and test stablecoin and tokenization initiatives. Last month, the central banks of Malaysia and Thailand joined Singapore's BLOOM initiative to work on cross-border payments involving stablecoins and tokenized deposits.

Japan's top financial regulators are also studying tokenization of Japanese government bonds and a blockchain-based settlement system for stocks and Japanese government bonds. South Korea, meanwhile, is preparing tokenized securities from 2027 and local won stablecoins under its draft Digital Asset Basic Act.

Earlier this month, the central banks of the UK, Singapore, and Thailand also said they completed foreign exchange settlement trial linking traditional and tokenized systems.

Ethereum’s Co-Founder Takes On Crypto’s Next Security Threat. Who Is Vitalik Buterin?

📅 Nov 27, 2026  |  Category: Technology  |  Read Source →

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

Who is Vitalik Buterin, and why is Ethereum’s co-founder now questioning the security of the very devices crypto investors use to protect their wealth? The 32-year-old programmer has turned his attention to a problem that even open-source software cannot necessarily solve: compromised computer chips.

In an essay published on November 26, Buterin argued that cryptocurrency security needs to extend beyond software and into the physical hardware on which it runs. His message builds on one of crypto’s oldest principles, but with a new twist:

For someone who helped build an alternative to centralized financial infrastructure, questioning the manufacturers behind that infrastructure seems like a natural next step.

It also reflects a security philosophy that has become increasingly visible in Buterin’s work, from his push for greater privacy and quantum safety on Ethereum’s roadmap to his interest in independently verifiable computing.

Vitalik Buterin is a Russian-Canadian programmer, researcher and writer who conceived Ethereum in 2013, at the age of 19.

Born in Russia in 1994 and raised in Canada, Buterin discovered Bitcoin in 2011. He went on to co-found Bitcoin Magazine, where he explored the technology and economics behind cryptocurrencies long before digital assets attracted mainstream financial institutions.

His involvement in Bitcoin exposed him to a problem that would eventually lead to Ethereum. Blockchain technology had potential beyond transferring money, but building more sophisticated applications on Bitcoin presented technical limitations.

Rather than trying to accommodate every possible application within Bitcoin’s existing architecture, Buterin began working on a blockchain designed specifically for programmability.

At the time, he was studying computer science at the University of Waterloo, where he also worked as a research assistant to cryptographer Ian Goldberg.

According to the University of Waterloo, Buterin received a $100,000 Thiel Fellowship in 2014 and subsequently left university to work on Ethereum full-time.

In November 2013, Buterin wrote the initial draft of what would become the Ethereum whitepaper.

The proposal described a blockchain with a general-purpose programming environment. Developers would no longer need to create an entirely new network every time they wanted to build a decentralized application.

Consider a lending platform. Instead of relying on a bank to manage collateral, calculate interest and authorize withdrawals, developers could encode those rules into smart contracts running on Ethereum.

That does not eliminate every risk. Smart contracts can contain bugs, depend on unreliable external data or operate under centralized administrative controls. What Ethereum introduced was the ability to execute financial and other programmable agreements on a shared blockchain.

Although Buterin originated the concept, Ethereum was not built by him alone. Its founding team included seven other individuals: Gavin Wood, Joseph Lubin, Charles Hoskinson, Anthony Di Iorio, Mihai Alisie, Jeffrey Wilcke and Amir Chetrit.

The project’s first live network, known as Frontier, launched on July 30, 2015.

What began as an experimental computing platform eventually became the foundation for much of the decentralized finance industry. Stablecoins, decentralized exchanges, lending protocols and tokenized financial assets now use the infrastructure that Buterin and Ethereum’s early contributors helped establish.

The network’s own evolution, particularly its transition to proof-of-stake and the development of Layer 2 scaling networks, has shaped Ethereum’s first decade.

A hardware wallet is supposed to keep private keys away from potentially compromised computers and smartphones. But what happens if the device itself cannot be trusted?

Buterin’s latest research examines that possibility. He points to supply chain attacks involving tampered wallets and considers the potential for malicious modifications concealed inside apparently legitimate chips.

Open-source firmware allows researchers to examine the instructions a device runs. But those instructions reveal little about whether the manufactured chip has been altered.

Buterin wants manufacturers to disclose physical chip layouts, known as GDS files, so investigators have a reference against which to inspect actual hardware.

The distinction matters. Knowing what a chip is designed to do is not necessarily the same as knowing what the chip inside your wallet actually does.

One approach highlighted by Buterin comes from hardware security researcher Andrew Huang, better known as bunnie.

Huang has been developing a technique called Infra-Red, In Situ inspection (IRIS), which exploits the fact that silicon becomes transparent at certain infrared wavelengths.

Using infrared illumination and suitable imaging equipment, researchers can examine parts of a chip’s internal structure without necessarily removing it from its circuit board.

The technique could help detect substituted components or unexpected differences between manufactured chips and their intended designs.

In a 2024 update on his research, Huang explained that infrared imaging has resolution limits. It cannot reliably reveal every microscopic feature of modern chips. Combining imaging with additional electrical testing could improve confidence in a component’s integrity.

That is an important limitation for crypto investors. Publishing an open hardware design does not automatically make a wallet secure, just as publishing a smart contract’s code does not establish that it is free of vulnerabilities.

Buterin acknowledges that sophisticated hardware inspections are more likely to be performed by specialist organizations than ordinary wallet owners.

His essay is a proposal for improving security, not an announcement that existing hardware wallets have all been compromised.

Despite his status as Ethereum’s most recognizable co-founder, Buterin is not its CEO.

Ethereum is maintained through the participation of independent developers, researchers, node operators, validators and other ecosystem contributors. Changes to the network involve technical proposals, discussion, software development and adoption by participants.

Buterin has considerable influence over those discussions, but publishing a proposal does not give him the authority to implement it unilaterally.

His role within the Ethereum Foundation is also distinct from control over the blockchain itself. In its April 2025 governance announcement, the Foundation described Buterin’s responsibilities as providing technical and intellectual guidance to the wider ecosystem.

His research can influence the direction Ethereum takes. Whether the network ultimately follows that direction depends on considerably more than his endorsement.

Buterin accumulated considerable wealth through his involvement in Ethereum, with much of his publicly visible cryptocurrency wealth tied to ETH.

However, his exact net worth is not publicly established.

Blockchain analytics can estimate the value of assets held in wallets attributed to him, but those figures do not necessarily account for all his investments, liabilities, private assets or holdings at addresses that have not been publicly identified.

They also fluctuate with cryptocurrency prices. A wallet valuation should therefore not be confused with a complete assessment of his personal wealth.

Buterin’s latest essay is part of a longer-running interest in making digital infrastructure independently verifiable.

In September 2025, he published The Importance of Full-Stack Openness and Verifiability, exploring how transparency could extend across the hardware and software underpinning increasingly important parts of people’s lives.

His broader research includes cryptography, privacy, blockchain scalability and Ethereum’s transition toward greater quantum resistance. Buterin has previously called for greater experimentation across Ethereum’s application layer without compromising its core principles of censorship resistance, open-source development, privacy and security.

These interests share a practical concern: whether users can independently establish that the systems they rely on behave as intended.

There is a commercial obstacle, though. Semiconductor manufacturers invest heavily in proprietary processes, and designing chips specifically for inspectability can involve performance compromises.

But a device signing a cryptocurrency transaction does not necessarily need the computing power of a modern AI processor. That makes security-focused hardware a potentially useful starting point.

More than a decade ago, Buterin challenged the idea that blockchains should primarily be used to transfer money. His latest work challenges another assumption the industry has grown comfortable with: that trusting the code is enough.

For crypto investors, the next meaningful development may come from hardware manufacturers willing to make their products independently inspectable, rather than another software update promising greater security.

Save big on accessories and Xbox games with these deals

Even though Xbox consoles aren’t on sale, you can still save big on controllers, headsets, games and more with these Black Friday deals. Unlike with the PS5, Xbox consoles are still readily available and you can pick up an Xbox Series S or Xbox Series X if you want to play GTA 6 or any of this year’s other big launches.

For instance, you can pick up a digital copy of GTA 6 with an Xbox Wireless Gaming Controller for $122 at Amazon. If you already have the game, you can get a Razer Black Shark V3 wireless gaming headset for just $99 to experience all Vice City has to offer in virtual surround sound. Many of this year’s best games like Resident Evil Requiem, Pragmata and Ace Combat 8 are also on sale too.

Whether you’re new to Xbox and want to build out your game library or want to upgrade your console with some new accessories, now is the best time to do so. Here are the best Black Friday Xbox deals worth shopping right now.

The Xbox Series S is limited to 1440p output but still delivers fast loading, ray tracing, and high frame rates. It features a GPU with up to 4 teraflops of output, 10GB of RAM, and a 512GB SSD. This console has no disc drive; it's designed exclusively for digital games.

The Xbox Series X All-Digital is the same powerful console with two key differences. Firstly, it comes in an attractive Robot White hue, and it also lacks a disc drive, so it is designed solely for digital play. It's the perfect console for Xbox Game Pass players.

If you miss chatting with friends the old fashioned way on Xbox Live, then this keyboard accessory that attaches to your Xbox controller could be the perfect way to relive the glory days. It works with the Xbox Series X/S controllers as well as with older Xbox one S and one Elite controllers. There’s also a 3.5mm audio jack if you want to plug in a wired headset at the bottom too.

While the Xbox Series X25 Limited Edition console is hard to come by and expensive, this deal lets you celebrate Xbox’s big anniversary for less. The GameSir X5 Lite is officially licensed by Xbox and supports phones or even small tablets like the iPad mini. This mobile game controller has Hall Effect sticks and triggers to prevent stick drift and you can swap its face buttons to match your preferred layout.

Versatile, comfortable, and responsive, the Xbox Core Wireless Controller impressed us in our rigorous testing. This isn't just for Xbox — it's compatible with PC, Android, and iOS devices too. With its ergonomic design, textured grips, and a button to share screenshots with friends, it's a go-to for gamers everywhere.

The Arctis Nova 5 is one of the finest gaming headsets, and it's the highest-scoring headset we've reviewed. Compatible with PS5, Nintendo Switch, PC, Android, iOS and Meta Quest, its quick-switch 2.4GHz dongle and Bluetooth 5.3 enable you to effortlessly swap between devices. The sound quality is incredible, and the 360° spatial audio makes your gaming experiences even more immersive.

This modular wired controller lets you swap out its thumbstick modules completely tool free. It also has two remappable buttons around back along with trigger stops. The eSwap Pro has mechanical face buttons too as well as a mechanical D-pad for enhanced precision, comfort and control. You may be tethered to your Xbox, but you’ll have pro-level control in the games you play.

This wireless headset is available in black or white and lets you connect to your Xbox, PC or smartphone using the included 2.4 GHz Hyperspeed Wireless Gen 2 dongle, Bluetooth or over USB-C. The BlackShark V3 also has a detachable Super Wideband mic and delivers excellent virtual surround sound on both Xbox and PC. It's worth noting that the black version is only slightly discounted at $127.

Grand Theft Auto VI + Xbox Wireless Gaming Controller: was $144 now $122 @ Amazon

This bundle gets you a copy of the standard edition of Grand Theft Auto VI alongside an Xbox Wireless Gaming Controller in Carbon Black. Normally, GTA 6 would cost $80 on its own while the controller would cost $65 so you’re actually saving quite a bit with this deal. You also get to play the biggest game of the decade with a brand new controller too.

The Nacon Revolution X Unlimited Controller is a high-end pad designed for the Xbox Series consoles and PC. It packs pro features like hall effect sticks, adjustable triggers, mappable back buttons, a customizable LC screen, and a rechargeable battery. At $199, it's not a cheap investment, but if you take your Xbox gaming seriously, it's a worthwhile upgrade.

The Turtle Beach Stealth 700 Gen 3 may be a tad bulky, but it delivers outstanding sound quality and a reliable microphone, making it a standout gaming headset. This is an ideal headset for multiplatform users thanks to its dual USB transmitters and fantastic onboard options. It’s one of the best Turtle Beach headsets you can buy, and it can be yours for under $200.

Sonic Racing: CrossWorlds is one of the most memorable entries in the Sonic the Hedgehog series. Packed with chaos, fun, and a bit of a learning curve, CrossWorlds shines with smooth drifting and air tricks that deliver significant boosts.

The latest game in the Mafia series takes you back to 1900s Sicily, the birthplace of organized crime. You play Enzo, a fresh recruit in the Torrisi crime family, and must work your way up the ranks to become a "made man." Offering a narrative-driven campaign packed with third-person firefights and high-speed chases (in cars and on horseback), Mafia: The Old Country is a highly engaging action-adventure game.

Assassin’s Creed Shadows delivers on its promise of bringing back classic stealth mechanics while introducing new ones and combining the best of the older and RPG titles. The detailed open world of feudal Japan feels alive, with compelling playable and non-playable characters, and varied fighting tactics enrich the combat. But the game struggles to balance its two playable protagonists, and player choices are still inconsequential.

Resident Evil Requiem combines elements from prior installments to deliver one of the strongest entries yet. Though it doesn’t take risks, its thrilling gameplay and stunning graphics keep you engaged from beginning to end.

Pragmata is a breath of fresh air thanks to its tactical combat, clever puzzles, and earnest sci-fi story. It proves that there's still innovation in the AAA space and is yet another winner from Capcom. This is a game that humans and androids alike can enjoy.

Star Wars Zero Company is a new turn-based tactics game where you recruit and lead a squad of operators and experience an original Star Wars story set during the Clone Wars. Offering strategic combat, cinematic production values, and a focus on player decisions, it's one of the best Star Wars video games in ages and a potential GOTY pick.

Lego Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight takes everything folks know about Batman from popular culture and filters it through the tried-and-true Lego formula. Whether you're a fan of Batman or Lego games, there's a lot to love in this charming adventure.

Control Resonant surpasses its excellent predecessor with a larger scope, both narratively and in gameplay. The melee-based combat is appropriately brutal and engaging, while the various skill trees offer deep customization. Aside from some confusing maps, this is an almost perfect action-based title.

The Blood of Dawnwalker is a dark, brilliantly written vampire RPG with a superb prologue, a memorable cast, and inventive powers. Repetitive combat, a rough performance, and an insipid lead drag it down at times. A flawed, fascinating debut with cult classic written all over it — one that needs some post-launch patches, but kept us hooked regardless.

Step into the cockpit, take flight, and prepare for battle in Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve, the latest installment in the popular aerial combat franchise. Boasting a full single-player campaign and the series largest suite of online modes to date, not to mention stunning visuals and sound, it's the complete Ace Combat package.

007 First Light is the finest James Bond video game in nearly 30 years. Its cinematic single-player campaign is remarkable, delivering a gripping, quintessentially Bond story paired with some of the best action-adventure set pieces we’ve ever experienced. Whether you’re a longtime Bond fan or a newcomer, 007 First Light is unmissable.

Crimson Desert is one of the most ambitious single-player open-world games ever. It throws a ton of deep systems at you with almost no hand-holding, but once it clicks, the combat feels fantastic, and exploration feels rewarding. There’s enough content here to keep you busy for months on end. The story is pretty average, and the beginning can be brutal, but if you love big sandbox adventures, this one is worth the ride (and $69).
